newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bomb hits St Petersburg metro, none hurt.
newsitem.headline: Bomb hits St Petersburg metro, none hurt.

text.p: A bomb exploded on the St Petersburg metro shortly after midnight on Thursday but no passengers were hurt badly enough to need hospital treatment, an official for the railway in Russia's second city said.
"It was obviously a terrorist act," Nikolai Savelev, an aide to the metro's director, told Reuters.

The bomb had been placed under a seat and blew up at eight minutes past midnight, blowing out the doors and windows of the second carriage of the train between Lenin Square and Vyborgskaya stations, northeast of the centre.
Interfax news agency quoted the driver of the train as saying there were only two passengers in the damaged carriage. One young man had been concussed.
The security services had started an investigation but Savelev said it was already clear the device resembled one which killed four people last June on the Moscow metro.
No one claimed responsibility for that bomb and there was no indication who might have arranged the blast in St Petersburg.
